answer_1.quote: We systematically evaluated watermark robustness using prompts across three domains: creative writing, education, and journalism... We generated watermarked texts (essays, news articles, stories) and applied perturbations.
answer_1.outputs: Watermarked texts, perturbed (unwatermarked) texts after random-walk attacks

answer_2.quote: We automatically evaluated text quality with several metrics. First, we used InternLM as a reward model to acquire a numerical quality score. We used GPT-2 to calculate perplexity... we counted grammar errors and computed unique bigram diversity.

answer_3.quote: We employed LLMs as quality oracles (e.g., Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, InternLM, GPT-4o) to decide whether a perturbation preserves quality... We also used Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, GPT-4o, and o3-mini-high as lineage distinguishers to attribute origin of texts.

answer_4.quote: Several coauthors, following standardized guidelines, compared perturbed texts to their originals, unaware of which was which... Annotators were provided with instructions: determine which is a better response to the prompt: text A, text B, or tie. Judge quality based on content, style, cohesion, and prompt relevance.
answer_4.guideline: Determine which response is better or tie, judging based on content, style, cohesion, and prompt relevance.
